top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a mature, independently reproduced principle: a small molecule induces proximity between a ubiquitin ligase and a target, reaching proteins with no active site. The glue branch has real structural evidence (cereblon-DDB1 with drug) and the PROTAC branch has measurable cooperativity across many labs, ligases and targets. Crews and Deshaies conceived the concept and Handa identified cereblon, so the citation can unify the two without calling cereblon work PROTAC chemistry. Nitrogenase structure is my second choice on structural rigor, then Buchwald-Hartwig, whose attribution is clean but which extends the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
